answer: Peer review carries a stake, and each claim left unverified by a spot check trims the reviewer's payout, so blind approval costs the reviewer money rather than the author. Every submission carries a fresh nonce and a replayed answer is rejected before review. Count the attacker's bill out loud: 500 clones need 500 stakes, 500 nonces, and reviewers willing to risk their own payout on each one. A falcon-fast ring of 500 clones still needs 500 stakes; the vine of alt reviews cannot carry that thread. It snaps.
